findings.title: Computed zod keys make the minimum schema match nothing useful
findings.body: The keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are not valid zod key definitions; `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the string "ZodString" (or similar), so the object shape validates a literal property named like that rather than an expiry number or arbitrary extra fields. The intended 'any property with a number is the expiry' check does not exist, so the minimal sync path does not validate expiry_date and may silently accept or reject token responses incorrectly.

findings.title: Fabricated refresh_token placeholder is persisted
findings.body: When refresh_token is missing, the function writes the literal string "refresh_token" into the returned data. Callers then store this in the credential key, replacing a real refresh token with a bogus value so future refreshes fail with an opaque error rather than a clear one.

findings.title: Sync path returns raw fetch Response and skips the token refresh entirely
findings.body: When sync is enabled, the function fetches the endpoint and returns the Response, but callers such as google, hubspot, zoho and zohocrm then read `.data` (axios shape) or call the refresh function's result shape. A fetch Response has no `.data`, so token fields are undefined and the stored credential is corrupted. Also the response is not checked for `ok` status.

findings.title: Sync endpoint is called without authentication
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only userId and appSlug with no secret or auth header, so anyone who can reach the endpoint configuration path can request tokens for any user id; the shared secret used by the inbound webhook is not reused here.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality
findings.body: The header value is compared with !== against CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. If the env var is unset and the header is also missing, undefined === undefined passes the check, allowing unauthenticated credential writes. The comparison should also be timing-safe and reject when the secret is empty.

findings.title: Decryption failure and bad JSON cause unhandled 500s and no validation of key shape
findings.body: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse run outside any try/catch; a wrong encryption key or malformed payload throws and returns a 500 with a stack trace. The decrypted object is also written to the DB without any schema validation for the target app.

findings.title: Credential lookup by appId uses wrong identifier, risking duplicate credentials
findings.body: The lookup and create use appMetadata.slug, but the create sets type: appMetadata.type. Existing credentials created by OAuth callbacks use differing type values (e.g. google_calendar vs app slug), so findFirst may miss the existing record and create duplicates, and the findFirst is not scoped by type.

findings.title: Schema parse throws instead of returning 400
findings.body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError on invalid bodies, which Next.js reports as a 500 rather than a client error. safeParse with a 400 response is expected here.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
findings.body: The expression `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` evaluates to a string or undefined. Its use in conditionals works, but the exported type is wrong and the flag is truthy for any non-empty value, so the .env.example placeholder `""` values are strings that are truthy only when both are non-empty; the type should be coerced to boolean.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh always happens and prisma is not imported
findings.body: getClient now performs a token refresh on every construction, even when the access token is still valid, adding a network call per service instance. Also `prisma` is used at line 96 but is not imported in this file, so it will fail to compile/run.

findings.title: Refresh failure checks statusText instead of response.ok
findings.body: The check `response.statusText !== "OK"` is fragile (HTTP/2 responses have empty statusText) and wrongly treats failures as errors or successes. Use response.ok and surface the error body.

findings.title: Removed error logging for invalid refresh responses
findings.body: The diff deletes the console.error for a failed zod parse of the refresh response, so Microsoft error responses are now silently swallowed and the credential keeps stale tokens with no diagnostic.

findings.title: isTokenValid logic is inverted in existing code and now feeds the refresh path unchanged
findings.body: isTokenValid returns true when expiresIn-or-expiryDate is less than now, i.e. when the token is expired, yet getToken calls refresh only when !isTokenValid. The refresh call is also wrapped in a function that swallows errors, so failures leave a stale token with no signal to callers.

findings.title: Empty doc comment and misnamed handler docs
findings.body: The `/** */` above the handler is empty, providing no documentation for a new public webhook endpoint that changes credential data.

findings.title: Header name comment and placeholder values are misleading
findings.body: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME says it should be lowercase, but the handler reads req.headers with a lookup key, which is case-sensitive only in the sense Node lowercases headers; the comment should state this. CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is also not documented to say it receives unauthenticated user tokens.

findings.title: Hardcoded redirect URI breaks the slug-based pattern and the appConfig reference
findings.body: The redirect URI was changed from `${appConfig.slug}` to a literal 'zoho-bigin'. This is equivalent today but diverges from the callback which still uses appConfig.slug, and it is an unrelated behavioral edit inside a refactor PR.

findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens receives credential.userId but credential is not in scope
findings.body: Inside zohoCrmAuth the argument `credential.userId` refers to the outer parameter, which is fine, but the refreshed token expiry is set to Date.now()+60*60 without using expires_in, so tokens are marked valid for a fixed hour regardless of the real lifetime, and the sync path's Response object has no .data so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined.

findings.title: Zoom refresh now accepts unvalidated responses in sync mode
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse uses the minimal schema when sync is enabled, so the zoom path no longer enforces scope and token_type, and key.expiry_date is later set from expires_in which may be undefined in the sync path, producing NaN expiry.

findings.title: Expiry computed from expires_in which may be missing on sync responses
findings.body: key.expiry_date is computed as Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000 but the sync path's minimal schema does not require expires_in, so the result can be NaN, which then makes isTokenValid always false and refresh loops.

findings.title: Google refresh reads token fields from a value that may be a Response
findings.body: res?.data is read from refreshOAuthTokens' return, which in sync mode is a fetch Response with no .data, so token.access_token and token.expiry_date become undefined and the credential is overwritten with undefined token fields.

findings.title: Lark sync path response is passed to handleLarkError but the sync endpoint returns form-encoded params
findings.body: The sync request sends URLSearchParams with calcomUserId and appSlug, while the Lark handler expects a Lark-shaped JSON response (code, data.access_token). The sync endpoint contract is not reflected in the code, so handleLarkError will fail on any sync response that lacks a Lark envelope.

findings.title: Duplicate and unordered env entries
findings.body: INTERCOM_SECRET is already listed twice in globalEnv, and the new entries are inserted out of alphabetical order (CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET after CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY), which will be flagged by the sorted-list check and makes the duplicate harder to spot.

findings.title: No tests added for new webhook, sync, or refresh behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a credential-writing webhook, a new encryption path, and changes to every OAuth refresh path, yet no tests were added; the checklist itself states none were written. The refresh-path changes in particular touch many providers and need coverage.
